//: PR CheckMate configuration template. Place this file at your repository root as 'pr-checkmate.json'. Every value below is the built-in DEFAULT — delete any block you do not want to change, because the file is deep-merged with the defaults. Keys starting with '//' are comments and are ignored. Full per-check reference: https://github.com/Mybono/pr_checkmate_public
//excludePaths: FILES AND FOLDERS NO CHECK EVER LOOKS AT, as globs: "src/generated/**" for a whole folder, "vendor/legacy.ts" for one file. Applied where every check gets its file list, so the rule is written once rather than per check. Use this before reaching for a per-check ignore; use 'ignoreDirs' only when you mean a directory NAME wherever it appears.
//1-scope: WHERE CHECKS LOOK. 'sourcePath' may be a string or an array. 'ignoreDirs' REPLACES the default ignore list rather than extending it, so copy the defaults you still want — the defaults cover build output, dependency and report directories, plus generated 'graphify-out'. Test directories are deliberately NOT in it: test code is still linted, type-checked and formatted, and is excluded per-check where it is noise (see 'duplicate', 'deadCode', 'diffSecurity' and the bundled cspell ignores).
//2-severity: UNIVERSAL ON/OFF SWITCH, keyed by a check's DISPLAY NAME (see //check-names below). 'off' removes the check before it runs; 'error' promotes a warning to a failure; 'warn' demotes a failure to a warning. This works for every check, including those with no 'enabled' flag of their own.

npm-audit.//auditLevel: info | low | moderate | high | critical. Only DIRECT dependencies at or above this level block. Default 'high': a moderate CVE often has no fix available, and blocking on it stops releases indefinitely for a risk most teams have already accepted. Set 'moderate' for a stricter line.
npm-audit.//ignore: Package names that never block, but are still reported as warnings.

//diffSecurity: 'ignorePaths' skips whole files by glob; setting it REPLACES the test-path defaults shown here, which exist because a security test's job is to contain the exact constructs this check hunts for. 'ignore' silences a finding LABEL everywhere instead. 'dataflowWindow' is how many added lines a value stays tainted for, so `const q = `...${x}`` on one line and `db.query(q)` on the next are still connected — a heuristic with no scopes and no reassignment tracking, so it only ever advises; 0 switches it off.
//sensitiveFileGuard: Flags .env files, private keys, CI config and lockfiles. 'ignorePaths' excuses ONE file by glob (a .pem test fixture); 'ignore' silences a whole CATEGORY and would excuse the next real key too — reach for ignorePaths first.

migrationSafety.//paths: Globs treated as migrations. Setting this REPLACES the defaults listed here.

dependency.//ignore: Dependency names, or globs over the whole name ("eslint-plugin-*"), that knip should ignore. Only applied when non-empty, and never when the repo ships its own knip config — that file stays the source of truth.

circularDeps.//: Circular imports (dpdm, bundled — nothing needed on the runner). Uses the project's own dpdm when it has one. When the analyzer cannot run, the check SKIPS rather than passing or failing.
circularDeps.//severity: Advisory by default: most repos carry long-standing cycles through barrel files. Set 'error' to gate merges on them.
circularDeps.//ignore: Globs over repo-relative paths to keep out of the analysis (generated or vendored code).
circularDeps.//timeoutMs: Cap on the analysis. On timeout the check skips rather than fails.

outdatedDeps.//timeoutMs: Cap on 'npm outdated'. On timeout the check skips rather than fails.

licenseCheck.//: GPL/LGPL/AGPL in PRODUCTION dependencies fail the run. Both lists below are APPENDED to the defaults.

vulnScan.//: osv-scanner, cross-ecosystem. OPT-IN: must be exactly true. Requires osv-scanner on the runner.

grypeScan.//: Anchore grype, cross-ecosystem. ON by default but skips when grype is absent from the runner.
grypeScan.//ignore: Suppress by CVE/GHSA id or by package name.
grypeScan.//timeoutMs: Cap on the grype scan. On timeout the check skips rather than fails. The scan never walks 'ignoreDirs' (node_modules, dist, …), which is what keeps it quick.

//bannedImports: Packages that must not be ADDED. Empty means the check is inert. severity defaults to 'warn'; use 'error' to fail the run.
//5-git-and-pr: Checks on the diff and on pull-request metadata.
//packageSize: Growth of the published npm package vs the last release. Advisory — a bigger tarball is usually earned. Only runs where package.json names a non-private package.

todoFixme.//requireTicket: When true, a TODO must reference a ticket id — '#123' or 'PROJ-456'.

largeFiles.//allow: Globs exempted from the size limit. APPENDED to a built-in lockfile allow-list.

missingTests.//ignore: Globs that never require an accompanying test. Setting this REPLACES the defaults, which cover *.d.ts, index files and *.config.*.

//customRules: Your own regex rules run against added diff lines. Each needs 'name' and 'pattern'; optional 'message', 'severity' (error|warn), 'include', 'exclude', 'flags'.

commitlint.//ignores: Regex sources for titles to skip, e.g. release PRs.

symlinks.//: Whole-repo scan for tracked symlinks whose target does not exist.
symlinks.//severity: Advisory by default. Set 'error' to gate merges on a broken link.
symlinks.//ignore: Globs for links intentionally left broken (e.g. a fixture testing another tool's own broken-symlink handling).

duplicate.//ignore: Test and mock paths are excluded by default because test setup legitimately repeats.

deadCode.//ignoreFiles: REGEX sources (not globs), matched against reported file paths. Setting this REPLACES the defaults.

coverage.//: OPT-IN: must be exactly true. Reads an existing coverage summary; it does not run your tests.
coverage.//reportPath: Path or array of paths to a coverage summary.

licenseHeader.//: OPT-IN: must be exactly true. Requires a header matching 'pattern' within the first 'lines' lines of each changed source file.

//7-linters: ESLint, Prettier, cspell and markdownlint. 'rules' blocks are MERGED with the defaults; 'ignorePatterns' and 'ignorePaths' are APPENDED.

cspell.//: Only "enabled" always applies. The rest configures the cspell config pr-checkmate generates, so it is ignored when the repository has its own cspell.json — that file wins.
cspell.//enabled: Set false to turn the Spellcheck check off entirely.
cspell.//words: Project vocabulary that should not be reported as misspelled. Appended to the bundled list.
cspell.//ignorePaths: Globs to skip, APPENDED to the bundled list — which already covers CHANGELOG.md (assembled from commit subjects, so its typos are unfixable), test and mock paths, lockfiles and minified bundles. Anchored to the repository root, so a pattern never matches a directory ABOVE the checkout.
cspell.//dictionaries: Extra cspell dictionaries to enable, on top of the bundled fr, ru, uk, he, es. Unknown names are ignored.
cspell.//language: Locales to spellcheck against. Omit it to keep the bundled "en,ru,uk,he,fr,es" — a value here REPLACES that list, so "en" alone reports every non-English word as a typo.

markdownlint.//ignores: APPENDED to the built-in list: node_modules, dist, coverage, graphify-out, .claude and CHANGELOG.md.

//7b-install: WHICH TOOLING IS FETCHED. The package ships ~233 MB and no repository needs all of it. "adaptive" (default) fetches only what this repository turns out to need; "eager" fetches everything up front, which is what a closed network or a prebuilt image wants and is also the exact previous behaviour; "manual" fetches nothing because the tools are already on the runner. A missing tool never fails silently: the affected checks skip with a reason in the report, or fail the run outright with onMissingTool: "error".

install.//profiles: Extra profiles beyond what detection concluded, for generated code or a monorepo layout detection cannot see through. Names: core, js, python, cpp, spellcheck, markdown, commitlint, duplicate.
install.//excludeProfiles: Never install these, even when the language is detected. Wins over 'profiles'.
install.//minFilesPerLanguage: Source files a language needs before its toolchain is worth downloading. Separate from detect.minFiles: running a check that then skips is free, downloading a toolchain is not.
install.//reuseLocal: compatible | always | off. Run the tool the REPOSITORY already has instead of our copy. "compatible" (default) does so when the major matches ours, or when the tool reads the repository's own config — a legacy .eslintrc can only be read by the ESLint it was written for, and a tsconfig.json by its own compiler. "always" reuses across a major gap at your own risk: our generated flat config does not load in ESLint 8. "off" always uses our pinned copy, for reproducibility.
install.//onMissingTool: auto | skip | error. In a closed contour a silent skip is not acceptable — use 'error'.
install.//offline: Forbid every network install at run time. Pre-warm with: npx pr-checkmate install --all
install.//cacheDir: Where fetched tooling is kept; the path includes the pr-checkmate version. Cache it in CI or the tooling is fetched on every run.
install.//deny: Packages never fetched, whatever profile asks for them.
install.//prewarm: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — accepted and ignored. Warming the cache needs a postinstall hook, and there is nothing to warm while every profile's tooling ships inside the package. Documented as inert rather than quietly doing nothing.

//8-languages: Language is auto-detected. A check skips when its language is absent, and runner-dependency tools skip when the binary is missing — so leaving everything enabled is safe. TypeScript and JavaScript have no block of their own: configure them through 'eslint', 'prettier' and 'typecheck' above.
//detect: HOW that auto-detection reads the tree, when 'languages' is not set explicitly. Generated reports, vendored code and marker files are already excluded; these knobs are for the cases the built-in rules get wrong in your repo. 'minFiles' is how many source files a language needs to count (a marker file such as pyproject.toml includes it regardless). 'excludePaths' ADDS to the built-in exclusions rather than replacing them. 'disable' drops a language outright.

python.//typeChecker: mypy | pyright — pins one checker. Leave unset: the runner's own mypy is used when it has one, our bundled pyright otherwise.

shellcheck.//: Needs the `shellcheck` binary on the runner; skips when absent.
shellcheck.//minSeverity: error | warning | info | style. Omit to keep ShellCheck's own default (every level).
